label: Formulated the decolonial phenomenology of racial subjugation
description: Fanon developed decolonial phenomenology to expose how systemic colonial racism shatters the corporeal schema of the colonized, creating an epidermal racial schema of alienation.
historicalContext: Articulated in Black Skin, White Masks (1952) while Fanon studied psychiatry at Lyon, drawing upon clinical case studies and lived existential experience.
dialecticalTension: Exposes the Eurocentric limitation of classical phenomenology by showing that bodily being-in-the-world is racially stratified under colonialism.

citations.author: Frantz Fanon
citations.sectionOrPage: Ch. 5 (The Lived Experience of the Black Man)
citations.quote: In the white world, the man of color encounters difficulties in the development of his bodily schema... Below the corporeal schema I had sketched a historico-racial schema.

citations.author: Lewis R. Gordon
citations.work: Fanon and the Crisis of European Man: An Essay on Philosophy and the Human Sciences

label: Engaged with Sartrean existentialism and the dialectic of anti-colonial struggle
description: Fanon utilized Sartre's phenomenology of the Look and Being and Nothingness, while Sartre famously composed the incendiary preface to Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth (1961).
historicalContext: Met in Rome in 1961 for intense philosophical debates on existential freedom, Marxist historical stages, and revolutionary violence.
dialecticalTension: Fanon critiqued Sartre's 'Black Orpheus' for reducing the Negritude movement to a mere transitional moment in a universal class dialectic.

citations.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
citations.work: Preface to Frantz Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth
citations.quote: The European has only been able to become a man through creating slaves and monsters... Fanon reveals the third phase: the native arms himself.

label: Synthesized psychoanalysis with social and political critique
description: Fanon applied psychoanalytic models of neurosis, projection, and the unconscious to diagnose the collective sociogenic pathologies produced by colonial domination.
historicalContext: As chief of psychiatry at Blida-Joinville Hospital in Algeria, Fanon developed 'sociogeny'—the principle that psychic disorders can originate in oppressive social structures.
dialecticalTension: Challenged Freud's individualist and purely ontogenetic psychoanalysis, arguing that colonial pathology is fundamentally sociogenic.

citations.author: Frantz Fanon
citations.quote: Beside phylogeny and ontogeny, there is sociogeny... society, unlike biochemical processes, does not escape human influence.

label: Expanded double consciousness into global anti-colonial revolution
description: Fanon deepened Du Bois' concept of double consciousness and the Veil into an existential analysis of the psychological fracturing caused by white colonial supremacy.
historicalContext: Du Bois and Fanon were key intellectual presences at the First Congress of Black Writers and Artists in Paris (1956).
dialecticalTension: Transformed Du Bois' psychological and sociological color line into an internationalist revolutionary struggle.

citations.author: Frantz Fanon
citations.quote: The black man has two dimensions. One with his fellows, the other with the white man... That this self-division is a direct result of colonialist subjugation is beyond question.

citations.author: Manning Marable
citations.work: W.E.B. Du Bois: Black Radical Democrat

label: Influenced theories of institutional discipline, biopolitics, and madness
description: Fanon's institutional psychiatry at Blida-Joinville and analysis of colonial disciplinary power influenced French post-structuralist inquiries into madness, medicalization, and state violence.
historicalContext: Foucault read Fanon during his early psychiatric research in the 1950s and during the Algerian War, shaping his anti-institutional perspective.
dialecticalTension: Connected colonial carceral techniques with domestic European disciplinary institutions.

citations.author: Ann Laura Stoler
citations.work: Race and the Education of Desire: Foucault's History of Sexuality and the Colonial Order of Things
citations.quote: Fanon's insights into the racialized anatomy of power anticipated Foucault's later formulation of biopower.
